description: Engines, clocks, tools, mechanisms, electricity, and robots, plus the physics they lean on: heat, energy, waves, sound, and feedback. Intelligence and computing have their own clusters.

concepts.title: Machines
concepts.summary: Parts arranged so that energy goes in, constraints shape it, and repeatable action comes out. Every machine is a chain of decisions about what may move and what may not.

concepts.title: Engines
concepts.summary: Fuel burns. Hot gas expands. Pressure pushes a piston, a crank turns the push into rotation, and valves time the cycle so it repeats. A large share of the energy always leaves as heat.

concepts.title: Efficiency
concepts.summary: No heat engine turns all its heat into work. The limit is set by the temperature difference. Everything else is friction, vibration, and heat that can be reduced but never removed.

concepts.title: Steam Engine
concepts.summary: Boil water, let the steam push a piston, condense it, repeat. It moved coal from mines, drove factories and trains, and started the industrial age long before anyone had a theory of heat.

concepts.title: Combustion Engine
concepts.summary: Burn the fuel inside the cylinder rather than in a boiler, and the engine gets small and light enough for cars and aircraft. Intake, compression, power, exhaust: four strokes, repeated thousands of times a minute.

concepts.title: Thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Born from the question of how much work an engine can do, it became the study of heat, energy, and probability. Its laws say energy is conserved, that entropy rises, and that you can't quite break even.

concepts.title: Heat
concepts.summary: Energy on the move because of a temperature difference. It's the random jostling of atoms, and it always flows from hot to cold unless something pays to push it back.

concepts.title: Temperature
concepts.summary: A measure of how energetically the parts of something are jiggling, on average. It decides which way heat flows, and there is a coldest possible value, absolute zero, where the jiggling nearly stops.

concepts.title: Energy
concepts.summary: The one quantity that can change form but never be created or destroyed. Motion, heat, light, chemical bonds, and mass itself are all energy in different clothes.

concepts.title: Clocks
concepts.summary: Stored energy in a spring or weight is released in small, equal steps by an escapement. An oscillator sets the pace. A clock keeps time by making motion regular.

concepts.title: Escapement
concepts.summary: A small rocking part that lets a gear train advance one tooth at a time. Its steady tick-tock is the sound of energy being released in equal, controlled bites.

concepts.title: Oscillation
concepts.summary: Anything that swings back to where it started can count. Pendulum, balance wheel, quartz crystal. The trick is a motion so steady it can be trusted as a unit.

concepts.title: Waves
concepts.summary: A disturbance that travels without carrying matter along. Water, sound, light, and quantum states all ripple this way, and the same few equations describe them all.

concepts.title: Resonance
concepts.summary: Push a swing at just the right rhythm and small pushes add up to a large motion. Every object has natural frequencies, which is why a voice can shatter glass and a bridge can shake itself apart.

concepts.title: Frequency
concepts.summary: How many times something repeats each second. It sets the pitch of a sound, the color of light, and the ticking speed of a chip, and it's measured in hertz.

concepts.title: Fourier Transform
concepts.summary: Any signal can be built from plain sine waves of different frequencies. Taking a sound or image apart that way is one of the most useful tricks in mathematics, and it sits inside compression, radio, and medical scanners.

concepts.title: Sound
concepts.summary: Pressure waves in air, or in anything else that can be squeezed. Pitch comes from how fast they repeat, loudness from how big they are, and the ear turns the difference into something we call music or speech.

concepts.title: Timbre
concepts.summary: Why a violin and a flute sound different playing the same note. The mix of overtones changes, and the ear reads that mix as the character of the instrument or voice.

concepts.title: Time
concepts.summary: The thing clocks count. We live it as a flow, physics folds it into spacetime alongside three dimensions of space, and thermodynamics gives it a direction.

concepts.title: Calendar
concepts.summary: Time cut into days, months, and years by watching the Sun and Moon, then argued over and patched for millennia. Every calendar is a compromise between astronomy and convenience.

concepts.title: Ageing
concepts.summary: The slow accumulation of wear that living things can't fully repair. It's entropy seen from inside a body, and it gives time its personal, felt direction.

concepts.title: Tools
concepts.summary: A lever, a wedge, a wheel. Each turns a small movement into a larger one, or a slow force into a fast one. Tools extend the body, then quietly change what the body expects to do.

concepts.title: Leverage
concepts.summary: Trade distance for force, or force for distance. The work stays the same. The mechanism only chooses how it arrives.

concepts.title: The Wheel
concepts.summary: Rolling beats dragging. It's one of the simplest ideas and one of the last to arrive, and it needed an axle to become the ancestor of gears, pulleys, and turbines.

concepts.title: Mechanisms
concepts.summary: Input, constraint, transfer, output. A mechanism forces motion down a narrow path so that one action reliably becomes another. Understand the constraints and you understand the machine.

concepts.title: Gears
concepts.summary: Wheels with teeth that mesh. They pass rotation from one shaft to another and, by differing in size, trade speed for turning force, which is how a small motor can move a heavy load.

concepts.title: Feedback
concepts.summary: A system that measures its own output and adjusts. A thermostat, a governor on a steam engine, a person steering: feedback is how machines, and living things, stay on course.

concepts.title: Firearms
concepts.summary: At a high level, a cartridge's chemical energy becomes rapidly expanding gas that accelerates a projectile down a barrel, while the rest of the mechanism contains the pressure. The engineering can't be separated from safety, law, power, and harm, and those are the parts I care about here.

concepts.title: Electricity
concepts.summary: Charge in motion, and energy that can be sent along a wire and turned into light, heat, motion, or thought. It moved power out of the factory and information out of the wire.

concepts.title: Electromagnetism
concepts.summary: Electricity and magnetism turned out to be one force: a changing electric field makes a magnetic one, and back. That loop is what light is, and it is how generators and motors work.

concepts.title: Circuits
concepts.summary: A closed path for current, with parts along it that resist, store, or switch. Arrange enough of them cleverly and you get amplifiers, radios, and computers.

concepts.title: Batteries
concepts.summary: Chemistry that holds energy in reserve and releases it as current on demand. Their limits, weight and charge time, quietly set how portable most modern devices can be.

concepts.title: Wireless
concepts.summary: Sending signals through space with radio waves instead of wires. The same trick carries broadcasts, phone calls, Wi-Fi, and the faint pulses from spacecraft.

concepts.title: Robots
concepts.summary: Machines that sense, decide, and act. What separates a robot from a machine with a switch is the loop: it measures the world, and the measurement changes what it does next.

concepts.title: Sensors
concepts.summary: Devices that turn some feature of the world, such as light, motion, heat, or pressure, into a signal a machine can read. They are a machine's senses, and their limits set its picture of reality.
